Subject: MSA and on-prem addendum — escrow and audit questions

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're moving towards an internal approval for a private on-prem deployment of Redwood for a pilot environment. Attached is our proposed on-prem addendum and a short SOW (Acme_OnPrem_Addendum_Draft.docx). Legal surfaced a couple of asks we wanted to confirm with you before we submit redlines formally:

- Source / artifact escrow: We need a mechanism to be able to run the product locally if Redwood goes insolvent or discontinues support. Our initial ask is for a source escrow with a third-party agent and a 30-day release trigger on insolvency or failure to meet SLA.
- Audit rights: We request the right to audit for compliance with encryption and data residency — ideally quarterly with 30 days' notice.
- License scope: Clarify whether the Order Form license permits running in customer-managed cloud/on-prem, and whether cross-subsidiary use is allowed.
- KMS and keys: Do you support customer-managed keys (BYOK/HSM) for private deployments? If not, what are the alternatives?

Could you point us to Redwood's standard redline position for these items, or suggest compromises? Happy to set a call this week. I'm looping procurement on this message.

Thanks,
Julia Nguyen
Director, Platforms & Integrations
Acme Health

Hi all,

I've reviewed the addendum and the points Julia raised. High-level positions we intend to propose in our redline:

1) Escrow scope: Redwood will agree to escrow the following with a mutually agreeable third-party escrow agent: (a) compiled container images and signed release artifacts; (b) build scripts and a runbook necessary to deploy the versioned images to an environment consistent with the production baseline. We will not place unrestricted source code into escrow.

2) Release triggers: Escrow release will be limited to (i) Redwood insolvency or bankruptcy; (ii) material and continuous failure to meet SLA for >90 days after notice and cure period; (iii) a court order. We will push back on a 30-day release without a cure period.

3) Audit rights: Customer audits will be permitted with 45 days' notice, limited to verification of encryption in transit/at rest, retention policies, and operational controls specific to the customer's instance. Audits will be executed by a mutually approved third-party auditor and limited to once per rolling 12 months unless there is cause.

4) License scope: Order Forms will grant a non-exclusive, non-transferable license to run the specified version(s) within the customer's environment and affiliated subsidiaries listed on the Order Form. No sub-licensing or broad redistribution.

5) Keys and KMS: Redwood supports customer-managed keys via BYOK with integrations to common HSM/KMS vendors. For on-prem customers we can support either customer HSM or Redwood-managed keys with envelope encryption; we'll require a written KMS operational attachment.

I'll prepare a redline set (Redwood_MSADefault_Redlines.docx) and circulate. Marcus, please enumerate the minimum artifact set we can confidently escrow. Stephanie, please attach the SOC2 mapping and any logs/retention statements we can share.

-Rishi

Rishi — thanks for the clear framing. A few follow-ups from our side:

- Escrow scope: Our security and IT teams are not comfortable with compiled-only escrow unless the build process and all third-party dependencies are fully captured. If you insist on excluding source, we need at minimum: signed container images, immutable image registry snapshot, all build-time artifact hashes, a documented list of third-party dependencies and versions, and a complete runbook. We would also like the release trigger to include a failure-to-patch critical security vulnerabilities for 60 days.

- Release timeline: 90 days after notice + cure is long for us in a clinical setting. Can we discuss a 30-day cure for critical failures and 60 days for non-critical?

- KMS: We prefer customer-controlled keys (BYOK) with hardware-backed key material. If Redwood requires envelope keys, we need clear guarantees and access controls documented.

Looping in Mike (outside counsel) to help with exact language. Attached are Acme's proposed redlines to the addendum.

Thanks,
Julia

Hi Julia & team,

Thanks for the detail. Some clarifications from Security:

- BYOK/HSM: We support customer-managed keys for on-prem and VPC options. For on-prem we can onboard a customer HSM (PKCS#11) and integrate with the deployment so key material never leaves customer custody. For VPC/private cloud we support customer-managed KMS through external endpoints and envelope encryption.

- Escrow artifacts: Our standard compromise is to escrow: (1) signed container images; (2) a cryptographic manifest of artifact hashes; (3) build scripts and a makefile-level runbook sufficient to rebuild artifacts from captured dependencies; and (4) an immutable snapshot of the image registry. We will not escrow proprietary source control history.

- Release triggers: Security supports a split cure window: 30 days for critical security failure (P0/P1 that Redwood fails to remediate), 60 days for non-critical continuous SLA breaches. Escrow release would additionally require confirmation from an independent third-party escrow agent and an insolvency/court trigger where applicable.

- Audit evidence: We can provide SOC2 Type II summary, encryption-at-rest configs, and a redacted operations runbook. Full production logs contain customer PII and are not shareable; we can provide scoped log samples and aggregated metrics for audit verification.

I'll attach a short evidence summary for your audit team. Happy to jump on a call to walk through specifics.

-Stephanie
Director of Security | Redwood Inference
